email.body1:
Pedram, saw Blackstone backed NetBrain at a $750M valuation to fund global expansion.

An expansion mandate like that usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for NetBrain off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Pedram, quick follow-up for NetBrain.

After a backing like Blackstone's, growth expectations jump faster than headcount can, and most teams cannot say how many meetings they actually need to hit the new number. The gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings NetBrain needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Pedram, last bit of proof for NetBrain.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to the CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how NetBrain's reply rate likely compares to other network and infra vendors. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Pedram, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. The stretch right after new backing is its own kind of busy and I get it.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a global expansion motion? I will tailor it to NetBrain either way.
